riley (ml-eng): Nightly eval spike — dialogue-safety pass rate dropped 8% vs yesterday. eval-bot attached the failure summary. :eyes:

eval-bot: nightly-run/1842009700 finished. suite=dialogue-safety, baseline_pass=92%, current_pass=84%, failed_prompts=4/120. config: temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=None, seed=unset, sampler=stochastic. logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/logs/1842009700

ben (evals): Huh — our nightly config shouldn't have changed. I pulled the run meta and it shows seed=unset which means harness used time-based seeding. That can explain variance but not a sustained 8% drop on these particular prompts.

marta (ml-infra): There's a recent infra change: commit 8f3a2b in infra-config bumped default temp in runner from 0.75 -> 0.8 and also switched sampler backend from 'legacy' -> 'hybrid-sample'. I'll paste the diff snippet: 
```diff
--- a/infra/runner/defaults.py
+++ b/infra/runner/defaults.py
@@
-DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.75
-DEFAULT_SAMPLER = 'legacy'
+DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.8
+DEFAULT_SAMPLER = 'hybrid-sample'
+DEFAULT_RNG_SEED = None  # previously 42 for nightly reproducibility
```

jason (serving): oof. The 'hybrid-sample' uses a slightly different top-p clamp and a secondary reservoir sampler that changed tail behavior. Combined with a non-fixed seed that could nudge edge-case prompts over thresholds.

riley (ml-eng): Can someone repro locally with the new defaults vs pinned old defaults? Quick check: run the failing prompt set with explicit seed and older sampler. Command I used: 
```bash
python -m evals.run --suite dialogue-safety --prompts failing_prompts.txt --seed 42 --temperature 0.75 --sampler legacy
```
If that recovers pass rate then it's config drift.

ben (evals): Running now on my laptop, will report.

ci-bot: Started job reproduce-1842009800 on runner-10 (tag: gpu-small). ETA ~5m.

ben (evals): Quick result: with seed=42 + legacy sampler we get 91/120 pass (~75.8% for the subset, up from 67 previously). With seed unset + hybrid-sample + temp=0.8 it's 63/120. So both seed and sampler change matter.

marta (ml-infra): Next steps: revert the default RNG_SEED change (put nightly back to 42) and flag hybrid-sample as opt-in for now. I'll open infra PR to pin nightly runner config.

jason (serving): Also adding an integration test in serving that asserts sampler semantics don't change without a major flag. Minimal test: generate on 10 fixed prompts with seed=42 and compare ngram distributions. If drift > threshold, fail.

riley (ml-eng): Can we also add a quick eval harness patch to always send explicit sampler + seed in the job payload (even if they match defaults)? That will prevent silent defaults from drifting.

marta (ml-infra): Yep, will add override in job spec immediately. Patch plan: revert infra defaults, add explicit fields in job dispatch, and run a full nightly rerun.

ben (evals): Filing issue: #EV-542 — "Nightly: sampler/default-seed drift caused regression in dialogue-safety". Assigning to infra + evals.

riley (ml-eng): For triage, let's also bisect the infra change window to confirm 8f3a2b is root. Steps: 
```
git checkout infra-config
git bisect start HEAD 8f3a2b~5
# run the small reproduce job each step (script included)
```

marta (ml-infra): I'll do the bisect on CI so we don't block local machines. Will post commit sha if confirmed.

jason (serving): Note for the record: quantization experiments earlier this week touched the inference kernel but those are gated behind dedicated/deploy flags — not nightly. I don't think quantization is in play here.

riley (ml-eng): Good. Once infra PR lands, let's rerun the nightly and check pass rates + attach eval diffs. Also add a short postmortem if it stays resolved. Thanks all. :+1:

eval-bot: comment: linked issue EV-542 created by ben. CI rerun queued.
